'''Tristen Jamal Newton''' (born April 26, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina Pirates]] and the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]].

==High school career==
Newton played at [[Burges High School]] in [[El Paso, Texas]], where his team routinely traveled great distances to play top teams in the large metro areas of Texas. Newton scored 3,266 points in high school and led the state in scoring as a senior at 37.2 [[points per game]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.courant.com/2023/01/28/confidence-is-key-for-uconn-point-guard-tristen-newton-and-dan-hurley-thinks-hes-unlocked-it/ |title= Confidence is key for UConn point guard Tristen Newton and Dan Hurley thinks he’s unlocked it |first=Joe|last=Arruda|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=January 28, 2023|access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Newton found success at East Carolina, entering the starting lineup as a freshman and averaging 11 points and 3.7 assists per game. He set the Pirates' program record for assists in a season by a freshman.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.reflector.com/sports/ecu-hoops-finishes-th-godwin-passes-leclair/article_7fce0866-d11e-53cc-9b14-ed08a1250918.html |title= ECU hoops finishes 11th; Godwin passes LeClair |work=[[Daily Reflector]]|date=March 8, 2020|access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref> He improved for his next two seasons, culminating in a junior season where he averaged 17.7 points, 4.8 rebounds and 5 assists per game. He was named to the All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) second team at the close of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://ecupirates.com/news/2022/3/9/mens-basketball-newton-named-to-all-aac-second-team.aspx |title= Newton Named To All-AAC Second Team|work=[[East Carolina Pirates]]|date=March 9, 2022|access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref>

Following the dismissal of his coach [[Joe Dooley (basketball)|Joe Dooley]] after the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]], Newton decided to transfer from East Carolina.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33730114/east-carolina-transfer-second-team-all-aac-guard-tristen-newton-commits-uconn |title= East Carolina transfer, second-team All-AAC guard Tristen Newton commits to UConn |first=Jeff|last=Borzello|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=April 13, 2022|access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref> He heard from over 30 schools after putting his name in the NCAA transfer portal, ultimately choosing the [[University of Connecticut]] (UConn), where coach [[Dan Hurley]] saw his playmaking as a missing piece for his [[Big East Conference]] team. Newton earned the starting [[point guard]] role and became the first player in program history to record two [[triple-double]]s. At the close of the season, Newton helped lead the Huskies to the sixth Final Four in school history and later, with a double-double, to UConn's fifth NCAA championship in [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/sports/college/2023/04/01/after-move-to-uconn-burges-tristen-newton-final-four/70070096007/ |title= ‘Ready for a stage like this': After move to UConn, Burges' Newton plays in Final Four |first=Quinton|last=Martinez|work=[[El Paso Times]]|date=April 1, 2023|access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref>

Newton returned to the program for the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] after initially declaring for the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Newton opts out of NBA draft, returns to UConn |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/37767865/tristen-newton-withdraws-nba-draft-returns-uconn |website=ESPN.com |language=en |date=May 31, 2023}}</ref> During a game against [[Manhattan Jaspers men's basketball|Manhattan]], Newton notched his third triple-double of his career with the Huskies, becoming the first player in program history to do so.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borges |first1=David |title=UConn men's basketball rolls to win as Tristen Newton sets record with third triple-double as Husky |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/article/manhattan-huskies-tristen-newton-18511504.php |website=CT Insider |access-date=November 25, 2023 |date=November 24, 2023}}</ref> He notched his fourth triple-double of his career against [[2023–24 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]], becoming the first power conference player to have four or more triple-doubles since [[Shaquille O'Neal]] got six.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dayton |first1=Kels |title=Tristen Newton’s name now next to Shaquille O’Neal, David Robinson on NCAA’s all-time triple double list |url=https://www.courant.com/2024/02/29/tristen-newtons-name-now-next-to-shaquille-oneal-david-robinson-on-ncaas-all-time-triple-double-list/#:~:text=Newton's%20four%20triple%20doubles%20are,posted%20four%20career%20triple%20doubles. |website=Hartford Courant |access-date=April 15, 2024 |date=February 29, 2024}}</ref> In the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], he led the Huskies to back-to-back championships, was named the [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] (MOP) of the tournament, and became a member of the [[Huskies of Honor]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tristen Newton inducted into Huskies of Honor upon arrival back at Gampel with champion UConn men |url=https://www.courant.com/2024/04/09/tristen-newton-inducted-into-huskies-of-honor-upon-arrival-back-at-gampel-with-champion-uconn-men/ |website=courant.com |language=en |date=April 9,
